mix_frequency_estimate: CALL ~80% / RAISE ~20% (raise reserved for KT-suited / Tx-with-FD blocker-combos; pure AdKd lives in the CALL slice)
reasoning:
Per-villain composition first. MP opens 2.5bb from ~15% range (broadways, pairs 66+, suited connectors 76s+, AK/AQ). On QJ9 MP cbets only 26% pot — a small-sizing range-bet that keeps MP's whole continuing range intact: overpairs AA/KK/QQ, the JJ/99 set portion (TT 3-bet sometimes), top-pair Qx, the J9/Q9/QJ two-pair sliver, plus the natural straight combos KT/T8s. Crucially MP's 26% sizing is NOT polar — it includes AhX/KhX type backdoor floaters and underpairs like 77-88. So MP's range at this node is broad but tilted toward made hands that beat AKo (Qx+, overpairs, sets, straights, two-pair). CO is the more dangerous range. CO flatted MP's open in a squeezable seat with hero+blinds behind, so CO's range is range-capped (no AA/KK/AQs+ — those 3-bet) but DENSELY concentrated in hands that smash QJ9: TT, 99, JJ-some, 88-TT suited, QJs, JTs, T9s, T8s, 98s, 87s, KTs, KQs, QTs, J9s. After MP's small cbet, CO's continuing range is heavy on Jx+, pair+gutter, T-x straights, and the JT/T9 combo-draw suite. CO calling small in front of hero advertises a strong continue range — hero is sandwich-disadvantaged in the sense that CO is uncapped-strong-relative-to-hero even while range-capped vs MP.

Hero AdKd equity-realization analysis. Nut gutshot (4 outs to T for nut straight, though T also gives CO a higher straight when CO holds KT — but KT is unlikely from CO who'd 3-bet KTs sometimes), plus two overs that are dirty (A and K both produce villain two-pair against Jx/Qx), plus the diamond backdoor (2-card BDFD, ~4% to hit runner-runner). Raw equity vs the MP-cbet × CO-continue joint range is roughly mid-30s — respectable but driven mostly by the gutshot, with overcard outs heavily discounted in 3-way because someone usually has a Q or J.

IP-closing dynamics. Hero closes the action — squeeze pressure is zero, no villains left to act, so CALL realizes equity cleanly. Pot odds 2.5 into 9.5 = ~21% needed, and hero clears that on gutshot+BDFD alone. Implied odds on the T are large: stacks are deep relative to flop pot, and a T gives hero the absolute nuts against TWO ranges that contain dominated straights (KT for hero vs T8/T9/QT/98 for villains) plus sets that pay off. Multi-villain composition: a raise must charge BOTH MP and CO out, but neither folds — MP continues with Qx+/overpairs/sets/straights/two-pair, CO continues with the entirety of the dense Jx-plus/draws/straights range described above, and worse, a hero raise polarizes hero into KT/sets-of-bluff while AdKd is the textbook bluff-raise candidate that gets blown off equity when 3-bet by a slowplayed straight or set. Raise also bloats the pot OOP-of-equity vs a range that has us crushed in its made-hand portion.

CALL keeps MP's bluffs and floats in, keeps hero's range uncapped, preserves the nut-straight implied odds, lets hero realize the gutshot+BDFD with position, and avoids the dominated-equity disaster of raise-getting-3-bet by CO's KT/JJ/QJ/T9 holdings. The ~20% raise slice belongs to KTs/T9s/JTs-blocker combos that have hand-class equity AND remove villain straights — AdKd is not in that combo group. Verdict: CALL, HIGH confidence.
